text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dayton peace agreement is in crisis but there is no alternative to it, Michael Steiner, deputy to the International High Representative Carl Bildt says.
- Draft laws concerning central bank and flag of Bosnia have been adopted by the Council of Ministers and country's inter- ethnic parliament to approve them on its session at April 8, Steiner says.
- A Moslem house was torched in Bosnian Croat-held town of Jajce by unknown perpetrators who later tried to rape its owner. Local police say the woman is now in hospital.
- Plan to restore joint Moslem-Croat police in divided Bosnian town of Mostar fails after Croat member refuses to sign agreement citing technical reasons.

- International supervisor for disputed Bosnian town of Brcko, Robert Farrand, is due to assume his post by the end of the week. Bosnian Croats threaten to obstruct supervision if the main check point for the town is not placed in their territory.
- There will be either a whole Bosnia or new war will break out, U.N. special envoy for human rights in former Yugoslavia Elizabeth Rehn says, dismissing possible division of country.

- Future of divided Bosnian town of Mostar is crucial issue for country considering how much money the European Union has invested in reconstruction. But certain political and religious leaders oppose normalisation, Rehn says.
- Croatian flag was spotted hanging on destroyed mosque in central Bosnian village of Ahmici, the site of a massacre where Bosnian Croats killed 117 Moslem civilians on April 16, 1993.

- Bosnian Serb decision to adopt unified customs law with Yugoslavia is a blow to efforts to pass package of economic reforms proposed by International Monetary Fund, says Bosnian minister for foreign trade, Hasan Muratovic. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
